speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the two-year recidivism rate for inmates released from drug rehabilitation centres (DRCs) reaching the highest since 2015 (a) what factors have contributed to the rise in the recidivism rate; (b) whether the Ministry is reviewing the effectiveness of rehabilitation programmes within DRCs; and (c) where do drug abusers obtain their supplies from and whether the increased accessibility to drugs has contributed to the increase in recidivism rate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Repeat drug abusers have a higher likelihood of reoffending and this may have contributed to the increase in the recidivism rate of DRC inmates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singapore Prison Service (SPS) regularly reviews the DRC regime to ensure it remains effective in addressing the drug abusers’ risks and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Drug abusers obtain drugs from various sources, including through platforms like Telegram and WhatsApp.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To curb the accessibility and supply of drugs into Singapore, the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) regularly orders online platforms to take down material advertising the sale of controlled drugs and takes tough action against drug traffickers as well as syndicates operating from overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: CNB will continue with its robust enforcement efforts to stem the supply of drugs and keep Singapore drug-free.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Minister of State mentioned that repeat drug abusers have a higher likelihood of reoffending.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are two-year recidivism rates of those with drug antecedents compared to those without drug antecedents?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And recognising that re-integration into society is critical for preventing relapse, what post-release support systems are currently in place for former DRC inmates and how does the Ministry collaborate with community organisations to ensure continuous support?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And are there plans to expand these initiatives?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look at the release cohorts over five years, you can see that the recidivism rates are also different, about three times more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if you look at those without drug antecedents, so, for the 2018 cohort, with drug antecedents, it was 29.9%, and without drug antecedents, it was 11.6%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For 2019, with drug antecedents, it was 27.4%, compared to without drug antecedents, it was 9.8%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For 2020, with drug antecedents, it was 26.9%, without drug antecedents, it was 9.4%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For release cohort 2021, with drug antecedents, it was 29.2%, and without drug antecedents, it was 9.4%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And the recent one, for release cohort 2022, with drug antecedents, it was 29.7%, and without drug antecedents, it was 9.8%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, with this we know the harms that drugs do to individuals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is about reaching out to the community so that we can help our people to stay away from drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I hope that we can get support from the House as well as society here in Singapore, fellow Singaporeans, because when you do not have a tough stance on drugs, it will seep into the society, it will break the society, destroy the society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many of my counterparts that I have met overseas shared with me, without them knowing, some of their countries have become a narco-state.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we want to make sure we help Singaporeans to have avenues for a pro-social quality of life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that we must make sure that while there are those who just do drug abusing, consumption, but we have seen how drug consumption have led to criminal activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, when someone is arrested, not only for drug consumption, but with some criminality aspect, it gets difficult and it gets more complicated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It will destroy the families, it will destroy the society, not only the individual.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I hope that we can work together on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While there are those who have been arrested for consumption or any related drug antecedent, we want to help them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are also religious programmes at the Re-integration Hub.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also have organisations, platforms like the Yellow Ribbon Community Project, Malay/Muslim Organisations Rehabilitation Network, Prison Fellowship, Hindu Centre, coming on board to help us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Recently, we also roll out the Desistor Network to get these desistors to play a part in this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is about enhancing all these efforts together so that we will continue to support them, even though they have taken drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They have abused drugs, they have committed an offence, but we want to provide them with second chances, so that they can build up their lives for better days ahead.
